title: Carbohydrate-responsive Element-binding Protein (ChREBP) Accentuates Mitochondrial Dysfunction via Modulation of Long Non-coding RNA Taurine Upregulated 1 (TUG1) in HIV-1-infected Macrophages
journal: American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine

sections.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title> <jats:p>Rationale: HIV infection leads to severe global public health issues. Although the widespread availability of highly active antiretroviral therapies (ARTs) has helped contain the HIV pandemic, viral persistence and entry to latency cannot be eliminated by ARTs. Transcription factor Carbohydrate-responsiveelement-binding protein (ChREBP) modulates metabolic genes in physiological and pathological contexts, including cancer and innate immunity. However, the mechanisms by which it modulates HIV-1 infection in macrophages are not well defined. We and others previously validated mitochondrial dysfunction in HIV-1-infected macrophages, affecting cellular metabolism that governs innate immunity. To investigate the role of ChREBP in the crosstalk of mitochondria and innate immunity, we analyzed the effect of ChREBP on metabolic genes in HIV-1-infected macrophages. Methods: HIV-1-infected human monocytes derived macrophages (MDMs) and chronically HIV-1 infected monocytes cell line U1 were used for related functional assays. CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockdown and activation strategies, antagomir, and mimics of microRNAs were utilized for gene gain or loss in MDMs. Target gene expression was detected through quantitative RT-PCR and immunoblot assay. Interactions among ChREBP/TUG1, TUG1/miR-22, and miR-22/PGC-1alpha were validated through luciferase activity assay, chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP), and RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP) assay. The effects of ChREBP expression on mitochondrial function were verified through a mitostress test and ATP production assay. Results: Elevated ChREBP and decreased TUG1 expression have been validated in HIV-1-infected MDMs. CRISPR silencing ofChREBP gene results in an increased lncRNA TUG1 and PGC-1alpha expression and reduced miR-22-3p and miR-22-5p expression. Metabolic analysis test showed that targeting the ChREBP gene modulated mitochondrial biogenesis in macrophages. Interruption of TUG1/miR-22 interaction decreased macrophageactivation, including interleukin-6 and TNF alpha. Furthermore, a ChREBP inhibitor SBI-993 partially alleviated mitochondrial dysfunction in MDMs caused by HIV-1 infection. The interactions among TUG1, miR-22, and PGC-1 alpha were confirmed through ChIP and RIP assay. Furthermore, overexpression of TUG1 via CRISPR activation effectively blocks HIV-1 reactivation. TUG1 silencing repressed PGC-1alpha expression and elevated miR-22 expression in macrophages. These findings were recapitulated in the HIV-1 latency TNF alpha-induced U1 cells and MDMs exposed to recombinant protein HIV-1 Tat and gp120. Conclusion: ChREBP /TUG1 is an upstream regulator of PGC -1alpha in HIV-1-infected macrophages and HIV-1 reactivated macrophages. ChREBP regulates mitochondrial biogenesisviaTUG1/miR-22/PGC-1alpha axis. These findings provide novel insights into the function of ChREBP /TUG1 axis in immune responses, suggesting a potential target for anti-HIV-1 therapies.</jats:p>
